text:
maria_s: Customers in APAC are seeing huge latency (600-1200ms) and intermittent 502s. Multiple reports that requests are landing in us-east instead of ap-southeast. Example account: acme-apac. Repro steps below, attaching curl + dig output. Escalating because this caused billing spikes from long-running retries.

support-bot: Incident INC-224567 created for APAC DNS routing. Priority: P2.

alex.b: Can you paste the exact curl you used and the client IP? also any auth errors in the logs?

maria_s: Curl I used (from customer's environment):

```bash
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" \\\"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

Response headers show `x-region: us-east-1` and round-trip ~820ms, body 502 in ~2% of calls. Customer-provided public IP: 203.0.113.45. No auth failures reported, just timeouts and retries.

lee_ops: 203.0.113.45 looks like an ISP/NAT address. Likely EDNS/Resolver rewrite so the authoritative GeoIP lookup sees the resolver (US) not client. That would route to US. Can you paste `dig +short @8.8.8.8 txt region.api.redwood.ai` or `dig +trace` from their network?

maria_s: dig output from their side:

```
; <<>> DiG 9.10.6 <<>> +trace api.redwood.ai
;; global options: +cmd
api.redwood.ai.	 60 IN A 34.235.120.12
;; Received 34.235.120.12 from 8.8.8.8#53(8.8.8.8) in 42 ms
;; auth server returning A record in us-east range
```

maria_s: traceroute to api.redwood.ai ends up at 34.235.120.12 (us-east) after a couple of hops.

lee_ops: That matches EDNS-client-subnet getting stripped by the ISP or the resolver. Our GeoIP fallback is then using the resolver's ASN/country, which is mapping to us-east. Short-term mitigations:
- Use X-Client-IP header if customers can provide it (we can trust if customer opts in).
- Add routing rule to prefer nearest region when measured latency > 250ms (safe fallback).
- Purge DNS prefill cache on affected APAC POPs so stale entries pointing to US are removed.

sre-david: Quick lookup: 203.0.113.45 reverse resolves to isp-proxy.example. GeoIP DB currently maps that ASN to US because of the proxy exit IP. Updating GeoIP DB likely won't fix because the resolver is doing the rewrite. I've opened INFRA-3241 to add resolver-affinity heuristics: if the resolver IP is in a known proxy ASN, prefer extracting X-Forwarded-For or fall back to latency-based routing. Traceroute snippet I ran from our APAC probe:

```
traceroute to 203.0.113.45 (203.0.113.45), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  1.2 ms
 2  100.64.0.1  12.3 ms
 3  34.235.120.12  120.6 ms (us-east edge)
```

alex.b: On billing — a few customers reported token usage skyrocketed because retries kept going to the slow US endpoints. We should proactively credit affected tenants for the spike and send a rollback notice. @finance / billing-team FYI.

oncall-andy: Deployed temporary routing change cfg-334 to prefer APAC when latency > 250ms or if header `X-Client-IP` present. Also purged DNS prefill for ap-southeast POPs (cache TTLs were prefill 3600s). Monitoring now.

maria_s: After that change, acme-apac test user measured latency drop from ~900ms -> ~120ms and 502s disappeared. Customer reported the improvement.

lee_ops: I'll follow up with product on adding a formally supported `client_ip_hint` header and update docs/SDKs. Also let's add telemetry to detect resolver-affinity mismatches (resolver ASN != client country and latency delta > 300ms).

sre-david: Filed INFRA-3241 and telemetry ticket TELE-2219. Will also check with CDN partner about prefetch/prefill behavior — prefill was contributing to stale routing.

alex.b: Billing credits request submitted for affected tenants (ACME, one-other). Support outreach message drafted.

maria_s: Customer confirmed billing adjustment and latency stable for 2 hours. Closing the incident after 24h of stable metrics. Thanks everyone for quick triage. :thumbsup:
